newsitem.title: CHINA: China's President Jiang hails HK handover triumph.
newsitem.headline: China's President Jiang hails HK handover triumph.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin hailed the Hong Kong handover as a triumph for the Chinese nation on Tuesday and said Hong Kong people would keep their freedoms and were masters of their own piece of China.

"This is both a festival for the Chinese nation and a victory for the universal cause of peace and justice," Jiang said in a speech accepting the 156-year-old British colony back at midnight on Monday (1600 GMT).
"July 1, 1997 will go down in the annals of history as a day that merits eternal memory.

"The return of Hong Kong to the motherland after going through more than a century of vicissitudes indicates that from now on, Hong Kong compatriots have become true masters of this Chinese land and that Hong Kong has now entered a new era of development," he said.

Jiang paid a warm tribute to Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, who died last February, for his creative genius in devising China's reunification strategy known as the "one country two systems" policy.
He thanked all in China and Britain who had translated the policy into Hong Kong's successful handover and welcomed Hong Kong's 6.4 million people into "the embrace of the motherland".
Hong Kong will now be called a Special Administrative Region of China, free to run all its own affairs except defence and foreign policy.

Jiang reiterated China's pledge under the 1984 handover treaty with Britain to leave Hong Kong's way of life unchanged for the next 50 years, with its own executive power, legislative power and independent judiciary.
Hong Kong people would keep their freedoms, he promised, and they would progress towards a suitable system of democracy, as envisaged under the post-handover constitution, the Basic Law.
"The Hong Kong SAR shall gradually develop a democratic system that suits Hong Kong's reality," Jiang said.

"The Chinese Government will unswervingly implement the basic policies of "one country, two systems", "Hong Kong people administering Hong Kong" and a high degree of autonomy and keep Hong Kong's previous socio-economic system and way of life unchanged and its previous laws basically unchanged," he said.
China would respect Hong Kong's economic independence and the economic interests of other countries in the territory.
